cards.text: This one's a song of ascents, and Israel gets told to say it out loud. Israel's line goes, "Many a time they have persecuted me from my youth". From YOUTH, friend. That's not a rough week. That's a rough LIFE.
Then Israel says that line again, word for word. It's like hitting the elevator button a second time. You KNOW it heard you. You just need it to know you mean it.

cards.question: Israel has been persecuted again and again since youth. The second time Israel says it, the line keeps going. How does it end?

answers.text: But they have not prevailed against me
And now I have nothing left to give
So I will hide from them forever

cards.question: Israel describes what all that persecution felt like. What picture does Israel use for its own back?

answers.text: A field the plowmen plowed over
A wall the builders tore down
A road the soldiers marched on

cards.text: And they made their furrows long. Not a quick pass. The WHOLE field. Meanwhile I spent a few years in the back of a junk drawer and thought I had it rough.
But right here, the song turns. Israel stops talking about the plowmen and starts talking about the LORD.

cards.question: After all those years of persecution, Israel calls the LORD righteous.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: Israel has been plowed over again and again. What does Israel say the LORD has done?

answers.text: Cut Israel from the cords of the wicked
Paid the plowmen back twice over
Given Israel a quiet field of its own

cards.text: Cords. Israel was tied up like a cookie box with the string knotted three times. And the LORD just goes... SNIP. Done. Next!

cards.question: Then the psalm turns to all who hate Zion. It says may they be turned back in ___.

answers.text: shame
peace
glory

cards.text: And the psalm has a picture for them too. May they be like grass on the rooftops.

cards.question: Grass on the rooftops ___ before it can grow.

answers.text: withers
spreads
flowers

cards.question: When the reaper comes by, the rooftop grass gives him a full armload to carry.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Not enough to fill the reaper's hands. Not enough for the binder of sheaves to scoop up. That's me opening the oven for a full tray and finding... one crumb. ONE. Just standing there in my apron like, "Where'd my batch go?"

cards.question: Last line. People walk past the ones who hate Zion. What does the psalm wish none of them would say?

answers.text: The blessing of the LORD be on you
Your fields will be full next year
Come and rest with us tonight

cards.text: Not even a "we bless you in the name of the LORD" from anybody walking by. The psalm wishes them no blessing at all.

findings.problem: The opening card has five sentences: 'This one's a song of ascents...', 'Israel's line goes...', 'From YOUTH, friend.', 'That's not a rough week.' and 'That's a rough LIFE.'

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'Then Israel says that line again, word for word.', 'It's like hitting the elevator button a second time.' and 'You KNOW it heard you. You just need it to know you mean it.' That is more than the 1 to 2 allowed.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The elevator comparison gives Israel a reason for repeating the line: 'You just need it to know you mean it.' The text never says why the line is repeated.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess the next words of a line: 'The second time Israel says it, the line keeps going. How does it end?' It should ask about the meaning instead, for example whether the persecutors won.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: 'Not a quick pass. The WHOLE field.' is told as if it were what the text says. Psalm 129:3 says only that 'they made their furrows long.' It doesn't say the whole field. The card also has four sentences.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: 'And they made their furrows long.', 'Not a quick pass.', 'The WHOLE field.' and 'Meanwhile I spent...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has five sentences: 'Cords.', 'Israel was tied up...', 'And the LORD just goes... SNIP.', 'Done.' and 'Next!'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke has the LORD saying 'SNIP. Done. Next!', which gives Him a brisk, offhand, service-counter attitude. It doesn't clearly target God, but it uses God's action for comic delivery.
findings.question: Is playful dialogue or attitude given to God, like 'Done. Next!', allowed under the reverence rule, or should humor stay off God's own actions and words entirely?

findings.problem: The question's own wording rules out the wrong answers. 'Grass on the rooftops spreads before it can grow' and 'flowers before it can grow' don't make sense, so only 'withers' fits 'before it can grow.' The wrong answers need to read as believable in the sentence.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The story card has six sentences: 'Not enough to fill the reaper's hands.', 'Not enough for the binder of sheaves to scoop up.', 'That's me opening the oven...', 'ONE.', 'Just standing there...' and the quoted line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
